market_holds: Spot about $50 (sealed 49.94; Yahoo bar about 50.3 intraday on 11-25), -16.4% over 20 sessions and -6.7% over 5, 0.2% above the 52-week low and 52% below the high. The run-in is mostly the tape: over the same 20 sessions GGAL fell 21.6%, BBAR 25.0%, SUPV 29.5%, ARGT 17.7% and SPY 7.2% (own arithmetic on Yahoo daily bars). So BMA has held up better than its peers, and it is the sell-side's favourite name (UBS's sector favourite, Goldman's highest projected ROE). The option chain cannot be used (ATM spread 112% of mid), there is no history in the baseline, and the deadband is 2.4%. Open reactions to the last four prints, own arithmetic: 3Q25 +2.2%, 4Q25 -2.1% (a 39% miss against Bloomberg consensus, -5.8% by the close), 1Q26 +1.8%, 2Q26 +0.1% (-3.1% by the close). Consensus: Bloomberg net income ARS 219.5bn, quoted 2026-11-13, roughly flat on Q2's 206.8bn reported and 221bn adjusted. Previews below it, published 2026-11-13: Citi ARS 188.5bn (-14% against consensus); Goldman expects recurring earnings to fall 19% in real terms QoQ, NIM to fall from 17.6% to 16.3%, ROE of 11.2% and NPL of 6.1%. The guide from the Q2 call is about 12% adjusted ROE for 2026 (9-10% reported), loans +2-5% real and NPL 5.5-6% by year-end, with management calling margins 'relatively resilient' for H2. The call is 2026-11-30, after the window, so any guide change lands outside it. The scored window spans a full Buenos Aires session on 11-26 (US Thanksgiving) and the US half-day open on 11-27.
view: Q3 2026 was a bad quarter for Argentine bank profitability, and the evidence says it was worse than the stale Bloomberg consensus. The BCRA's September Informe sobre Bancos puts system ROA for Q3 at 0.8% annualised (ROE 3.4%), against 2.5% in Q2, and blames mainly a lower total financial margin. Country risk rose from about 400bp in early July to about 600-640bp by early October, which marks down bond books. Supervielle, the one peer already out, halved its net income, cut its NIM by 430bp and cut its loan guide, and its ADR traded flat-to-weak against peers the next session. Citi and Goldman both sit 14-19% below the Bloomberg number. Against that, Macro is the best-capitalised and highest-margin name and has outperformed its peers on the way down, so the price holds less of a sector-wide miss for Macro than for the others. The release will most likely show net income below ARS 219.5bn and plausibly below Citi's 188.5bn, NIM compression and a reported ROE nearer 8-11% than the Q2 13.4%. That matters for the price mainly through relative positioning: Macro is the consensus 'quality' pick, and a print that looks like the system would undercut that. Against this: the previews were public 12 days ago, the stock sits at the lows and about 0.6x book, Argentine bank ADRs have shrugged off well-flagged bad quarters before, and the open is diluted by a full BYMA session plus the global tape. Lean down, not a bet.
unpriced: The Bloomberg consensus (219.5bn) is stale relative to the Q3 system data. The BCRA September report (system Q3 ROA 0.8% vs 2.5% in Q2) came after the 11-13 previews, and Macro's relative strength against peers suggests the market still treats it as insulated. It probably is not fully insulated, but that is only a partial gap: the sell-side previews already quantified a miss.

recommendation.reason: The evidence that the quarter misses the Bloomberg consensus is dated and fairly strong: BCRA system Q3 ROA 0.8% vs 2.5%, Supervielle's halved profit and 430bp NIM drop, Citi and Goldman 14-19% below consensus, and country risk up about 200bp inside the quarter. But the previews quantifying a miss were public on 11-13, the stock is at the lows near 0.6x book, and the window's open also carries a full Buenos Aires session and the global tape. So the probability that the direction is right does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Net income at or above roughly ARS 200bn with NIM holding near 17% (Macro's bond and dollar book carrying the quarter), which would confirm the market's 'insulated quality' view and likely produce a relief open like 3Q25 and 1Q26.

self_critique: The miss was flagged loudly 12 days ago by Citi and Goldman, and Argentine bank ADRs have a habit of rallying on well-telegraphed bad quarters (3Q25). At 0.6x book and at the 52-week low, an 'in line with Citi' print could produce a relief open. System ROA is pulled around by public banks, and Macro's dollar and bond book may have behaved differently from the system. The 11-27 open also embeds a full Buenos Aires session and the global tape (SPY has been swinging 2-4% a day), which can swamp a 2-3% earnings reaction. These keep the lean modest; they do not reverse it, because Macro's relative strength means its price has not absorbed a sector-like quarter.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was the most useful step: it showed BMA's fall was tape and that Macro outperformed its peers, so the drawdown is not a cushion. P4's 'previews quantify it' test is what kept this from becoming a recommendation. The thin baseline (no options, no history) meant the reaction history had to be rebuilt by hand.
